summary.en: Salvadoran forces are in Haiti searching for four missing soldiers after a gang ambush near Port-au-Prince, while Benin has pledged 2,000 troops to help combat gangs. Hunger is worsening as high food prices and El Niño persist, and the postponed presidential election is now set for July 2027. Bukele’s deployment of Salvadoran troops adds a foreign military element, and he has denied allegations of airstrikes by his forces. The United Nations reports 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Salvadoranske styrker er i Haiti og leter etter fire savnede soldater etter et gjengangrep nær Port-au-Prince, mens Benin har lovet 2 000 soldater for å hjelpe mot gjenger. Sulten forverres ettersom høye matpriser og El Niño vedvarer, og det utsatte presidentvalget er nå satt til juli 2027. Bukeles innsending av salvadoranske tropper tilfører et utenlandsk militært element, og han har avvist påstander om luftangrep fra hans styrker. FN rapporterer 193 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
